vision._tag_note: 2026-08-19: tag 52 relocated further toward the REAR of the robot, same 113 mm deck height (unchanged, per the operator). Re-measured with the same self-calibrating rotation method as 2026-08-14, extended to THREE readings instead of two: at rest, read the tag pose; rotate in place; read again; rotate again; read a third time. Least-squares fit of all three (x,y,yaw) samples to tag_world = centre + R(yaw)*(dx,dy) gives dx=-41.0 mm, dy=+0.5 mm, with residuals under 0.3 mm on every point; a held-out check using only readings 1-2 predicted reading 3 to within 0.68 mm. Sign matches expectation: negative x = behind centre, y approx 0 = on the centreline, matching the same-position mount reasoning used for gopiv's tag placement. CORRECTION to the note this replaces: the mobile-tag registration for tag 52 (x_mm=50.2, y_mm=-0.5, the front-mount values) was still present in list_mobile_tags after a fresh rogo daemon session and an AprilCam camera/detection restart -- registrations DO persist across restarts in practice, contrary to what was written here 2026-08-14; re-register after any physical remount regardless, since a stale registration silently reports the wrong centre. Also observed this session: the `turn <deg>` MOVE verb enqueued (ack OK, corr_id assigned) twice but the robot never actuated and the completion wait timed out both times, encoders unchanged; raw `wheels <l> <r> <ms>` teleop drove normally and was used for all three rotations instead -- a `turn`/MOVE-completion regression worth a firmware look, not chased down here.

geometry._trackwidth_note: trackwidth is the CALIPER-MEASURED wheel separation (stakeholder, 128 mm). Do NOT bend it to make turns land -- it is the one independently verifiable number in this file. Scrub correction belongs in calibration.rotational_slip; main.cpp derives an effective track = trackwidth / rotational_slip and hands THAT to Drive/Odometry/plannerLimits.
geometry._rotational_slip_note: 2026-08-09 REVISION, 0.9117 -> 0.9371 (stakeholder directive, out of process). Re-measured against the protocol-v5 MOVE angle-stop path (rogo turn, which stops on |encoder heading change|) over the getez radio relay, overhead AprilTag truth, 13 valid turns: +/-90, +/-180, +/-360 at 45/90/150 deg/s across two field positions 25 cm apart. EVERY turn OVER-rotated, 1.8-3.8%, and the error stayed a constant PERCENTAGE across magnitude, direction, speed and position -- so it is geometry, not a slip-rate effect (a 3.3x speed range moved it not at all). Effective track measured 136.59 +/- 0.58 mm against the 140.40 mm that 0.9117 implies; 128 / 136.59 = 0.9371. READ THE DISAGREEMENT WITH THE 2026-07-29 FIGURE BELOW BEFORE TRUSTING EITHER: that run measured the LEGACY open-loop turn path with host-side compensation and concluded 100.2% / 140.4 mm; this one measures the firmware's own encoder ANGLE stop and concludes 97.2% / 136.6 mm. Both are recorded deliberately; neither has been shown to supersede the other for the other path, and nobody has yet re-run the 07-29 protocol to see whether the robot itself changed. PRIOR: 2026-07-29, camera-measured on the playfield. Scrub: the ratio of ACTUAL rotation to what ideal differential kinematics (omega = (vR-vL)/b) predict -- a skid-steer robot drags its wheels sideways through a turn and under-rotates. 180 deg in-place turns vs overhead AprilTag truth, 3 W->N->E / 3 E->N->W: 180.3 deg actual (sd 1.9), 100.2%. Equivalent to an effective track of 140.4 mm against the measured 128. Domain {0} u [0.5, 1.0] (config.proto); 0 is the uncalibrated sentinel meaning apply no correction. Consumed at BOOT (gen_boot_config.py -> boot_config.cpp -> main.cpp kEffectiveTrack); a runtime CONFIG rotSlip patch acks ERR_UNIMPLEMENTED, so changing it needs a reflash.
geometry._rotation_calibration_note: 2026-07-29, camera-measured, robot untethered. Turn response is affine: actual = gain*commanded + offset, fitted over 48 shuffled in-place turns (15/30/45/90/135/180 deg, both directions, omega 2.5/4.5/6.5/8.0 rad/s). The SAME law holds at every rate -- accuracy does not degrade with speed, so this is geometry/stiction, not a dynamics artifact. The ~-6 deg offset is why small turns were so bad: a 15 deg command landed at 9. Inverting it (commanded = (desired - offset)/gain) and re-running 47 trials gave a residual of mean +0.64 deg, sd 2.13, max 6.5 -- verified at 8.0 rad/s as well as 2.5. SIGN MAPPING, confirm before trusting: these were measured in the camera frame, where POSITIVE commanded omega DECREASES yaw. _pos here = positive commanded omega (clockwise in camera), _neg = negative. NOT YET CONSUMED BY FIRMWARE: rotation_gain_pos/neg and rotation_offset/neg exist in msg::DrivetrainConfig but have no reader and no emitter in gen_boot_config.py -- dead data, exactly as rotational_slip was before this session. Compensation is currently applied host-side (scratchpad turn_verify.py) because the robot is on battery and cannot be reflashed; wire it up next time it is on the bench.

motors._port_note: tovez is wired port 1 = RIGHT wheel, port 2 = LEFT wheel. The generator default (left=1, right=2) made the firmware call the right wheel 'left', which negates every heading derived from omega = (vR - vL) / b while leaving forward motion correct -- so it never surfaced, and was patched three separate times downstream (navigator yaw_sign, planner applyOtosHeading negation, sim kOtosHardwareMountSign) instead of at the source. These MUST move together with the per-wheel calibrations below; swapping the values alone, with the ports fixed, inverts BOTH motors rather than relabelling them, which reverses forward as well as rotation (measured: a commanded +150 mm leg travelled -152 mm).
motors._vel_gains_domain: duty [-1,1] (NezhaMotor MotorVelocityPid); NOT the old PWM-percent scale
motors._vel_gains_note: 2026-07-15 RESONANCE TAMED (106-002, live config() gain sweep -- P4 binary wire, tests/bench/velocity_step_response.py, no reflash between trials): vel_kp 0.0014->0.0016, vel_kff 0.00135->0.0008. History: the ORIGINAL 0.0018 loop had a ~140 mm/s overshoot RESONANCE (+24..+33% on a velocity step); the 2026-07-12 interim detune (vel_kp 0.0018->0.0014, vel_ki 0.008->0.005, vel_kaw 15->20) only halved it (~+11%, still over the <~10% bar) and cost rise time. This session's own bench grid at kp=0.0014/kff=0.00135 measured worst-case +25% at 140mm/s (reproducing the historical pattern -- the interim detune alone did not clear the bar this session either). Root cause, found by exhausting kp/ki/kff/iMax/kaw per architecture-update.md (106) Decision 4: kff (feedforward) was OVER-estimated -- raising it (tried 0.0016) made overshoot WORSE (kff*target is an immediate open-loop kick added on top of kp*error, so an over-large kff over-drives the plant right at the step) -- confirming the 2026-07-11 kff derivation's own flagged 620-740mm/s measurement variance was real drift, not noise. Lowering kff to 0.0008 (with kp still at 0.0014) killed the resonance (worst 2.1%) but slowed rise time by ~30-50% (0.9-1.5s vs the interim's 0.9-1.28s) -- kp=0.0016 restores it: 3 consecutive full-grid confirmation runs all passed the <~10% bar with FASTER rise times than the interim detune (worst overshoot 9.3%/4.3%/5.0%; rise times 0.28-0.98s vs the interim's 0.9-1.5s) -- both overshoot AND rise time improved over the shipped interim, not just traded off. vel_ki/vel_kaw unchanged (0.005/20.0) -- the fix lived entirely in kp/kff, ki/kaw were not the lever needed this time. Re-verified from a clean reflash (boot defaults only, no live config() call) after persisting -- see 106-002's own completion notes for the full before/after table. Endpoint-accuracy re-verification (turn_sweep.py-style angle grid) NOT re-run this session -- flagged as a follow-up if endpoint regressions are observed, per the interim detune's own precedent of trading a little endpoint accuracy for trajectory smoothness. vel_filt=0.3 unchanged. See clasi/sprints/106-host-trajectory-planner-profiled-twists-straights-and-turns/issues/heading-loop-output-clamp-and-velocity-resonance.md's own Part 2 (marked resolved by 106-002) for the fuller history.
motors._vel_kff_note: 1/650 -- from duty-saturated plateau measurements 2026-07-11 (620-740 mm/s across windows; window-to-window variance cause not established -- NOT power, per stakeholder). Do not lean on FF accuracy: the loop should be feedback-dominant (see motion_control.ipynb verdict).
motors._vel_ki_note: kept 0.0018 in the 2026-07-11 session; motion_control.ipynb then showed the loop is FF-dominated with 40-50% step overshoot and weak steady-state correction -- a feedback-dominant retune (kp/ki up, acceptance via motion_control.ipynb) is the open next step.
motors._vel_filt_note: kept 0.3: raising to 0.6 (2026-07-11) cut measurement lag but pushed step overshoot to ~11% and turns to +6/+9/+7 -- the decel-lag surplus just became an overshoot surplus. 0.3 is the verified optimum of that trade with the current gains.

drive._shaper_note: decel-into-the-goal campaign (2026-07-22, follow-on to clasi/issues/angle-stop-overshoot-61-73-percent-on-hardware.md's own 'Option 1... remains the path to closing that residual further'): a_max/a_decel/j_max/yaw_jerk_max were dead data (orphaned by 115-003's motion-stack excision, gen_boot_config.py's own docstring documented them 'unread') until THIS campaign made them live again via Motion::VelocityShaper -- gen_boot_config.py's shaper_config_for_config() now reads all six of a_max/a_decel/alpha_max/alpha_decel/j_max/yaw_jerk_max into Config::ShaperBootConfig, consumed by App::MoveQueue to taper the commanded speed toward each Move's own stop threshold (a_max/a_decel/j_max/yaw_jerk_max source VALUES UNCHANGED, still 800.0/800.0mm/s^2 and 5000.0mm/s^3/100.0rad/s^3 -- carried forward, not retuned, since they were already reasonable bench starting points). alpha_max/alpha_decel are NEW this campaign (a_max/a_decel's angular sibling, no prior msg::PlannerConfig field to inherit from): alpha_decel=7.0rad/s^2 is derived from the taper-distance formula VelocityShaper itself implements (angle = omega^2/(2*alpha)) targeted at the ticket's own '15-20deg taper from omega=2rad/s (the TestGUI cruise rate)' bound -- 2^2/(2*7.0) = 0.2857rad = 16.4deg, inside that band. alpha_max mirrors alpha_decel (symmetric ramp-up/taper), matching a_max/a_decel's own symmetric 800.0/800.0 precedent. jerk-limited S-curve stage (same day, stakeholder correction): the shaper's own commanded ACCELERATION is now itself slewed by at most j_max/yaw_jerk_max per second (velocity_shaper.h's own file header has the full algorithm) -- j_max=5000mm/s^3 means a_max=800mm/s^2 is reached from rest in 0.16s; yaw_jerk_max=100rad/s^2 means alpha_max=7rad/s^2 is reached in 0.07s -- both plausible, not yet independently bench-retuned this campaign (carried forward from their pre-existing sprint-114 values).

drive._duty_per_speed_correction_note: 2026-08-03 (132-009, the-configuration-object.md / .claude/rules/configuration-discipline.md): corrected from the stale 0.00187325 this field carried since before 2026-07-31 to 0.001182, matching App::Drive::kDutyPerSpeed's own measured constant (drive.h) -- the value that has ACTUALLY been running on every robot's boot since 2026-07-31, because Configurator::install() (then boot_calibration.cpp's installDriveCalibration()) hardcoded that C++ literal and ignored this field entirely ('MEASURED, NOT CONFIGURED', stakeholder 2026-07-31 -- the ~1.6x error the-configuration-object.md's Cause section and this file's own _drive_calibration_note below both cite). 132-009 reverses that: Configurator::install() now reads duty_per_speed_left/right from THIS field, per the 2026-08-03 configuration-discipline rule ('every value the robot uses comes from the file'). This edit is BEHAVIOR-PRESERVING, not a new bench measurement -- it makes the file agree with what was already baked and running, closing the gap rather than re-deriving the number. Both fields are kept numerically EQUAL by convention (not independently re-fit against each other or against wheel_gain -- see _wheel_correction_note below for why that circularity is exactly what the 07-31 decision was guarding against, and Drive::kDutyPerSpeed's own doc comment, drive.h, for the full reversal reasoning). A fresh population duty-sweep (src/tests/bench/duty_sweep.py) is still the right way to supersede this number -- see ticket 132-019, the sprint's own hardware headline, which promotes whatever it measures back into this field per configuration-discipline's own bench-sweep protocol.
drive._drive_calibration_note: 2026-08-01 (130-001, population duty-sweep protocol): duty_sweep.py extended to the FULL duty range (0.04-1.0, was 0.04-0.60), per motor per direction, plus a simultaneous-both-wheels grid and a --from-csv refit path -- see the script's own header for the full protocol. Two corrections found and fixed in the tool itself: (1) it was inverting the duty axis off THIS file's duty_per_speed_left/right, which boot_calibration.cpp has ignored since 2026-07-31 (Drive::kDutyPerSpeed is now baked in firmware, config-independent) -- the tool now hardcodes the firmware's actual constant (0.001182) instead, cross-checked every run by a constant-free saturation reading; (2) the default fit window's upper bound (0.28, picked before this session's own full-range data existed) was too narrow, spanning only 3 near-breakaway rungs -- the LEFT wheel's complete curve (both directions, full range) shows genuinely linear behavior with a STEADY local slope of ~1000-1200 mm/s per duty all the way to duty~0.55 (NOT ~0.30 as 129-006 estimated from a 0.60-ceiling sweep), then a sharp one-rung collapse into saturation (peak 584 mm/s fwd @ duty 0.596 / 555 rev @ duty 0.545; 570/521 mm/s at full duty, only -2 to -6% off peak) -- 129-006's saturation-onset estimate was itself session-specific, not a fixed ceiling; the tool's default fit-duty-max is now 0.50. Refit over [0.12,0.50]: left fwd 1101.3 mm/s/duty (offset -14.2), left rev 1023.1 (offset +1.7) -- this SUPERSEDES the 129-006/06-issue figure of L 853.6 for the left wheel (that fit's 0.12-0.60 window, with no upper cutoff, blended the genuinely-linear region with the very onset of saturation at its top edge, biasing the slope down). SESSION FAULT, INCOMPLETE RIGHT WHEEL: the robot went hard-silent (no PING, no telemetry) after 45 good rungs, right-fwd duty=0.293 onward -- confirmed via read-only pyOCD halt+backtrace (core running, PC in RAM, spinning in codal::system_timer_wait_cycles/system_timer_current_time) and reproduced across 2 fresh reconnects including a hard DTR reset; matches the documented dead-motor-brick-battery/unpowered-external-I2C-bus signature (banner+frames then total silence, every reboot re-wedges), NOT a cable/USB-enumeration issue (mbdeploy list stayed healthy). Right wheel therefore has only 3 usable fwd rungs (duty<=0.242, fit gain 1197.8 mm/s/duty, LOW CONFIDENCE -- not re-verified against its own full range) and ZERO reverse or simultaneous-grid data this session; the OLD 129-006 R 837.8 figure is UNCONFIRMED, not superseded, pending completion. The parallel-lines/population verdict computed from this incomplete n=3 sample came out slope-dominated (fanned) -- OPPOSITE the stakeholder's intercept-only hypothesis -- but is flagged LOW CONFIDENCE for the same reason (the right-wheel line rests on 3 near-breakaway points) and must not be treated as settling Stage C's design question either way. Derived (report-only, NOT applied to any config key): biasMax +-23.8 mm/s (offset population envelope), vMin 99.7 mm/s (worst breakaway duty 0.09 x mean gain), breakaway band 0.04-0.09 duty (44-100 mm/s); candidate Stage-A wheel_gain/intercept-decel values per wheel/direction were also computed but, per this file's own _wheel_correction_note below, are NOT written here -- refitting that pair from bench/encoder data is exactly what that note warns against; camera-measured verification is still required first. Battery was NOT freshly charged or independently verified before this session (the robot has no pack-voltage telemetry, so charge state can only be inferred, not measured) -- given the session ended in a hard fault matching the known dead-battery/unpowered-bus signature, this raises 129-006's own flagged battery-artifact possibility from a soft caveat to the leading hypothesis for tonight's failure specifically (separate from, and not proof of, 129-006's ORIGINAL saturation/decline finding, which this session's own data already partially supersedes for the left wheel). The full population campaign (physically swapping motors) and a freshly-charged-battery re-run are BOTH deferred to the same stakeholder-scheduled follow-on bench session, which must ALSO complete the right wheel's full range and the simultaneous grid before any of tonight's derived constants should be trusted as final. Prior note follows, superseded where noted above: duty_per_speed_* [duty/(mm/s)]: open-loop wheel calibration, the inverse of the measured plant gain (speed_sweep 2026-07-27: L ~560, R ~510 mm/s per duty; ceiling ~500 mm/s). Per-wheel because the two gearboxes differ ~10%. crawl_pulse [-1,1]: fixed pulse amplitude for sub-breakaway wheel speeds, Bresenham-dithered in App::Drive; 0 disables. Measured breakaway is 1-6% duty and state-dependent (src/tests/firmware/duty_min/RESULTS.md) -- the earlier 0.20 was sized against a duty_sweep criterion that the standalone prober disproved, so crawl ships OFF pending a re-measure of the low end.
drive._wheel_correction_note: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-04 (132-019, the sprint's own hardware headline -- see below). Prior text, kept for history: 'IDENTITY as of 2026-07-31 (stakeholder). The fitted values (tovez: gain ~1.47) were measured against a duty_per_speed that was itself wrong by ~1.6x, so the pair was circularly calibrated -- each fitted against the other's error -- and the correction ended up pointing the WRONG WAY: it divided a 150mm/s request down to 96 before the duty conversion, on a robot that was already under-delivering. duty_per_speed is now a baked measured constant (App::Drive::kDutyPerSpeed), so this affine stage has nothing left to correct and is held at identity. Do not re-fit it against duty_per_speed again; refit only against camera-measured travel, and say so here. gain 1 / intercept 0 = no correction.'
drive._wheel_correction_132_019_note: 2026-08-04 (132-019, hardware bench acceptance, tovez, firmware v0.20260804.1): the circularity the note above warns about was specifically duty_per_speed and wheel_gain being fit AGAINST EACH OTHER while duty_per_speed was itself wrong (~1.6x, fixed by 132-009/duty_per_speed_correction_note above). With duty_per_speed now an independently-validated, UNCHANGED population constant (0.001182, matching Drive::kDutyPerSpeed's own hardware-measured saturation constant), fitting wheel_gain from ENCODER-measured plateau tracking (src/tests/bench/velocity_profile_gate.py) is a single-unknown fit, not a mutual one -- duty_per_speed is held fixed throughout, never re-derived here, so this does not reintroduce the 07-31 circularity. (The 07-31 note's suggestion to prefer camera-measured travel predates the duty_per_speed fix and predates this ticket's own explicit protocol -- sprint 132's the-configuration-object.md Verification section and this ticket's own Testing section both specify velocity_profile_gate.py, encoder-based, as the acceptance instrument.) Measured baseline (this session, tovez, direct USB /dev/cu.usbmodem2121202, firmware freshly reflashed from this sprint's HEAD): 5 back-to-back runs same boot (run1 cold through run5) showed a real cold-to-warm PHYSICAL convergence (bias resets to 0 on every reconnect -- see the DTR-reset finding below -- so this is genuine thermal/mechanical warm-up, not Stage C) from trapezoid L83.1/R70.8 (run1, cold) to L91.7/R80.7 (run5); square profile converged faster and more stably at L89.8/R79.3 by run3-5. Correction was computed as the AVERAGE of trapezoid+square plateau tracking at run5 (the most-converged point measured): left (91.7+89.8)/2=90.75% -> gain_left=0.9075; right (80.7+79.3)/2=80.0% -> gain_right=0.800. Both intercepts held at 0 (gain-only correction, per the-configuration-object.md's own design intent: ONE shared population-scale duty_per_speed, all per-wheel deviation expressed as wheel_gain/wheel_intercept). VERIFIED LIVE, SAME CONNECTION (src/tests/bench/output/019_sameboot_A_preop.{png,csv} vs 019_sameboot_B_postpush.{png,csv}): pushed via 4x set_config_field(DRIVE, wheel_gain_*), all acks ok, get_config(DRIVE) read back exactly what was pushed, unrelated DRIVE fields (duty_per_speed_left/right, crawl_pulse, all 4 intercepts) confirmed byte-unchanged. Same-boot before/after: trapezoid plateau L 89.6%->102.5%, R 78.6%->104.1% (gap 11.0pts -> 1.6pts); square plateau L 90.7%->101.3%, R 78.3%->101.9% (gap 12.4pts -> 0.6pts). The L/R GAP closed cleanly in both profiles; both wheels OVERSHOOT the 100% target (102-112%), most likely a combination of continued physical warm-up during the postpush measurement (it runs strictly after preop, so the plant is warmer) and ordinary run-to-run noise on a single ~1.5s plateau sample -- NOT chased further with additional tuning passes, per this ticket's own instruction not to tune until it looks good and report only the best run. IMPORTANT FIRMWARE-HANDLING FINDING, this session: SerialConnection.connect() over DIRECT USB pulses DTR on every open (serial_conn.py's own doc comment), which resets tovez's microcontroller -- confirmed empirically (a live-pushed DRIVE value read back correctly, then reverted to baked identity after nothing but a disconnect+reconnect, no power cycle). DRIVE is also NOT in Configurator::persistIfEligible()'s flash-persistence table (only WHEEL_CONTROL/MOTORS/OTOS are) -- a live DRIVE push is RAM-only BY DESIGN and cannot survive ANY reset, reconnect or power-cycle alike. This is why the values in THIS file (baked, reflashed) are the ones that actually ship -- the live wire push above demonstrates the wire capability and the gap-closing property, but only the baked path in this JSON satisfies 'survives a cold boot.' Cold-boot (post-reflash) verification numbers are in this ticket's own completion notes (clasi/sprints/132-.../tickets/019-....md), not duplicated here.

wheel_control._v_min_note: 2026-08-04 (post-133-004 bench, tovez, firmware v0.20260804.3, velocity_profile_gate.py, stakeholder-directed bake): was 99.7, the population breakaway figure derived in _drive_calibration_note (worst breakaway duty 0.09 x mean gain). Measured live-push A/B at the FINAL baked gains (kp=0/ki=6/iMax=60/pos_err_max=10): the floor was the entire trapezoid ramp excess -- 133-004's own open item. applySpeedFloor() boosts every sub-floor ramp command UP to v_min, and the sub-99.7 portions of the two ramps integrate to ~+37mm = +8.3% of the 450mm move: trapezoid delivered 110.4/110.9% at 99.7 -> 101.1/101.8% at 20 (repeat 102.0/101.8; v_min=0 gave 101.1/101.1, indistinguishable from 20). The square is untouched by the change (102-104% either way) because its 150mm/s plateau never enters the floor region -- which is also why the excess was profile-dependent. This SUPERSEDES 133-004's null v_min A/B (runs vmin0_kp1 vs kp1.0): that pair was taken in the kp-only regime where both arms read ~117% for a different reason, and the null was carried into a config where it no longer held. 20 rather than 0 keeps a nonzero boost for genuinely tiny STANDING commands (the sprint-114 dead-zone fix's intent) while getting the floor out of the way of deliberately-decelerating profiled ramps. CAVEAT, honestly: 99.7 was stall PROTECTION, and this bench cannot price that -- the stand's wheels are unloaded, so whether a loaded wheel stalls on ramp ends at floor 20 is UNMEASURED. If loaded driving shows ramp-end stalls, the right fix is the deferred planner-side one (sprint 131 Design Rationale Decision 4: the planner does not floor its own profiled ramps -- a decelerating profile is not a standing sub-breakaway command), not restoring 99.7 wholesale.
wheel_control._stall_note: 2026-08-08, stakeholder directive after the robot repeatedly drove into the playfield rails and ground there with nothing noticing. These three are DESIGN CHOICES derived from the drivetrain's own already-measured numbers, NOT a tuning sweep -- no stall was deliberately induced to fit them, and they are labelled as such rather than dressed up as measurements. stall_speed = 15.0 mm/s: encoder velocity at true rest reads ~0, so this only has to clear noise, and it sits well under the 20.0 v_min this robot ships. stall_demand = 40.0 mm/s: the floor above which a command is a genuine request for motion. Deliberately set ABOVE v_min (20.0) so applySpeedFloor()'s boost region cannot produce a stall candidate, and above the deadband so a standing sub-breakaway command -- which legitimately does not move the wheel -- is not read as a jam. stall_window = 500.0 ms: the sustain time, sized against planner.a_max = 300.0 mm/s^2. A healthy start from rest at that ramp passes stall_speed within ~50 ms and reaches 150 mm/s by 500 ms, so an honest acceleration has a full order of magnitude of margin and cannot trip this; a genuine jam holds the condition indefinitely. Reversals pass through zero speed only momentarily and are nowhere near the window. WHAT IS UNVERIFIED: the window has not been checked against a deliberately slow profiled ramp (a Move whose commanded speed sits just above stall_demand while the taper is still climbing), and the whole detector is inert on any robot whose JSON leaves stall_window at 0.
wheel_control._pos_err_max_note: 133-004 (2026-08-04, tovez, firmware built --clean --robot-debug, src/tests/bench/velocity_profile_gate.py; raw rows in src/tests/bench/output/133-004_summary.csv). SUPERSEDES the 133-002 seed note below, which said this field held 0 because tovez had no position-loop measurement at all. It now has one. pos_err_max = 10.0 mm is the BINDING SAFETY BOUND of the position I term, and it was set from the OUTPUT side after a direct sweep of it came back null. The direct sweep (runs `poserr1`/`poserr3`/`poserr10`, ki=6/iMax=100) returned rows indistinguishable from each other -- square 1.0411-1.0511, trapezoid 1.1011-1.1100, L/R 0.9968-1.0000 at every setting. That is a null result on PERFORMANCE and is reported as one rather than dressed up as a tuning win; the knob is nonetheless proven to have moved, because the firmware echoed `DBG:pos 1.000/3.000/10.000 applied` on each run. What actually resolved the quantity was the OUTPUT-side pair (`pe10_im40` vs `pe10_im100`, three interleaved repeats each): at iMax=40 the RIGHT wheel stayed clipped at 104.0-105.1% plateau tracking with square L/R stuck at 0.9832-0.9853, and at iMax=100 it reached 100.0-101.5% with square L/R 0.9916-1.0021. So the right wheel's genuine I demand EXCEEDS 40 mm/s -- the earlier, narrower `imax20`/`imax40` A/B located the knee too low and was superseded. Since the I term's ceiling is min(ki*pos_err_max, iMax), pos_err_max = 10 sets that ceiling at 6*10 = 60 mm/s, which covers the measured demand. CONFIRMED BY PREDICTION rather than assumed: run `pe10_im60` was taken to test the claim that iMax=60 must be identical to iMax=100 once ki*pos_err_max=60 is already binding, and it was -- square L/R 0.9894/0.9916/0.9916 against 0.9916/1.0021/0.9979, inside this rig's ~+-1% run-to-run scatter. pid_i_max is therefore set to exactly 60.0 = ki*pos_err_max so the two clamps agree and neither is decorative: a blocked or wedged wheel banks at most 10 mm of debt and draws at most 60 mm/s of unearned correction, bounded identically in both domains. NOTE the divergence from the source issue honestly: vevov used pos_err_max 5 with iMax 100, an inconsistent pair (ceiling 5*12=60 from the mm side, 100 from the mm/s side); this robot's pair is deliberately consistent. CAVEAT on the read-back path: the `DBG:pos` verb calls Drive::setPositionErrorMax() directly and does NOT update the struct that get_config(WHEEL_CONTROL) reports, so a DBG-pushed pos_err_max reads back as the BAKED value and velocity_profile_gate.py's i_term_hazard() warns `pos_err_max=0` on every live-pushed run. Baking it here is what makes it read-back-confirmable at all.
wheel_control._stage_b_tuning_note: 133-004 (2026-08-04, tovez): Stage B is LIVE for the first time on this robot. Every value below was measured on tovez in one bench session and each names the run that produced it; run tags are the `run` column of src/tests/bench/output/133-004_summary.csv and the full console log is src/tests/bench/output/133-004_gate_sweep.log. Method: velocity_profile_gate.py, both profiles, interleaved repeats, --tick 0.10 --lease 0.4 --attempts 8, direct USB to tovez by UID 9906360200052820a8fdb5e413abb276000000006e052820. BASELINE (run `b0_baseline`, all pid_* = 0, Stage B inert): trapezoid delivered/commanded L 1.1844 R 1.1511, square L 1.0956 R 1.0911, plateau tracking 107-110% -- the open-loop duty map over-delivers ~8% and nothing was closing it. pid_kp = 0.0, and this is a MEASURED RESULT, not a leftover zero -- it answers 130-004's Open Question 4 -- does the fast loop need a nonzero kp at all, given the profiler's every-tick re-plan-from-measured-position -- with a NO. The kp sweep was run first with the I term off (runs `kp0.5`/`kp1.0`/`kp2.0`): 0.5 under-corrected (plateau tracking L 106.1%), 1.0 reached L 105.4%, 2.0 reached L 103.9% but DESTABILIZED -- plateau sd jumped to 60.18/59.08 mm/s against 5.53/6.68 at kp=1.0, an order of magnitude of ripple for two points of tracking -- so 1.0 looked like the knee and was baked first. It was then withdrawn on evidence from the SIM, and re-tested on the robot. The sim's straight-leg crab regression (src/tests/sim/system/test_straight_leg_crab_regression.py, an ideal symmetric plant where a straight leg should not crab at all) measures max|cruise heading| = 0.1120 deg with Stage B inert; baking kp=1.0/ki=6 took it to 0.4477 deg, past the test's 0.3 deg bound, with cross-track from -0.40 mm to -2.51 mm. Bisected by disabling one term at a time: kp=1.0 with the I term OFF gives 0.5596 deg (fails), and kp=0 with ki=6/iMax=60 live gives 0.1120 deg -- EXACTLY the inert baseline. So the velocity-domain P term is the entire cause and the position-domain I term contributes nothing to it. The robot was then asked whether kp was buying anything at all (run `kp0_ki6`, three interleaved repeats, kp=0/ki=6/iMax=60/pos_err_max=10): square L/R 0.9979/1.0000/0.9957 and trapezoid 1.0020/1.0000/0.9960 -- indistinguishable from kp=1.0 -- while trapezoid plateau tracking IMPROVED to L 99.6-101.1% / R 100.6-101.8% against kp=1.0's L 101.8-103.2% / R 101.9-104.0%. kp=0 is therefore equal-or-better on every bench metric AND removes the heading regression, so it ships. The velocity P term is the knob that made the plateau rough and the heading wander; the position term is the one that does the work. This is the same asymmetry the source issue's investigator flagged as surprising -- more POSITION gain improved balance while every velocity-side knob misbehaved. pid_ki = 6.0 from the ki sweep (runs `ki3`/`ki6`/`ki12`, kp=1.0): ki=3 -> square 1.0489/1.0556, tracking 101.0-102.1%; ki=6 -> square 1.0411/1.0433, tracking 99.6-100.3%, L/R 0.9979; ki=12 -> tracking went ERRATIC (93.9%, then 106.9% on the repeat) and trapezoid plateau sd rose to 33.98-51.29 mm/s against 8.05-12.02 at ki=6. 6 is the measured optimum and is HALF the vevov figure of 12, which is visibly unstable on this loaded drivetrain -- the concrete reason the issue's bare-motor numbers were not transcribed. pid_i_max = 60.0, set to exactly ki*pos_err_max so the INPUT-side and OUTPUT-side clamps agree -- see _pos_err_max_note for the full derivation and for the prediction test (`pe10_im60`) that confirmed it. The first A/B on this knob (runs `imax20`/`imax40`, pos_err_max=5) showed 20 mm/s clipping the right wheel (R tracking 103.8/104.7%, L/R 0.9793) and 40 apparently clearing it, and 40 was baked on that basis; the wider three-repeat pair (`pe10_im40` vs `pe10_im100`) then showed 40 STILL clipping (R 104.0-105.1%, L/R 0.9832-0.9853) where 100 did not (R 100.0-101.5%, L/R 0.9916-1.0021). The two-point A/B had located the knee too low. Recorded rather than quietly overwritten, because the first bake of this file carried 40. pid_max = 100.0 is NOT a tuned value and is labelled as such: it was not swept. It is the value every measurement reported here was taken under, and it replaces 0, which in App::Drive::fastPid() means NO total-authority clamp at all (`if (gains_.pidMax > 0.0f)`); shipping a live P+I with an unbounded total was not acceptable. Tightening it is future work. pid_kaff = 0.0 is DELIBERATELY LEFT AT ZERO and is NOT a measured result: the ticket's own Open Questions 2 and 3 flag the cmdAccel/WHEELS path as unvalidated and note that the one prior sweep run on top of a nonzero kff returned ~50% dead runs, so raising it enters unvalidated territory. Untested here; still open. v_min = 99.7 is DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED and was NOT replaced with the vevov figure of 20: an explicit A/B at identical gains (run `vmin0_kp1`, floor disabled, vs run `kp1.0`, floor at 99.7) found NO measurable difference -- trapezoid 1.1700/1.1778 against 1.1644/1.1822, square 1.0967/1.1067 against 1.0767/1.0989 -- because both profiles' plateaus (150 and 200 mm/s) sit above the floor and it only ever engages on the trapezoid's ramp ends. This session therefore produced no evidence to move it, and its existing value is a population-measured breakaway figure for THIS drivetrain while 20 is a bare-motor number for a rig with essentially no rotational inertia. RESULT after baking (run `final_kp0`, three interleaved repeats, NOTHING pushed live -- every gain from the baked config): L/R imbalance closed from a +-3% spread at baseline to ~1.00 on both profiles, and plateau tracking from 107-110% to ~100%. WHAT STAGE B DID NOT FIX, and it is the honest headline: the DISTANCE ratio is barely moved on the trapezoid. Baseline trapezoid delivered/commanded was L 1.1844 / R 1.1511 and it is still ~1.104. Stage B fixed the plateau SPEED and the left/right SPLIT; it did not fix the trapezoid ramp excess, which is a different defect living in the ramps -- see the end of this note. WHAT IS STILL OPEN: the trapezoid still delivers ~111% against the square's ~104%, and that residual is NOT explained by the speed floor (A/B above) -- at command end the trapezoid is already ~108.6% while the square is ~99.6% with ~22 mm of coast after, so the trapezoid excess is inside the commanded window and lives in the ramps, where Drive::positionError() re-anchors to zero the instant commanded speed reaches 0 and discards exactly the debt accumulated during ramp-down.
wheel_control._wheel_controller_note: 2026-08-02 (130-004, wheel-speed-controller-moves-into-drive.md Phase 2): App::Drive's unified three-timescale controller. Stage C (bias trim) ships LIVE: wheel_v_min=99.7/wheel_bias_max=23.8 are ticket 001's own population-measured figures (2026-08-01 duty-sweep session) -- LOW CONFIDENCE (n=3, this robot's own two motors, one incomplete after a mid-session hardware fault; see tovez.json's control._drive_calibration_note for the full writeup). That same session's parallel-lines test came back slope-dominated (fanned), the OPPOSITE of the intercept-only hypothesis this Stage C design assumes -- flagged explicitly, NOT treated as settling the design question (ticket 001's own text: do not switch to slope adaptation on n=3). wheel_tau_adapt=30.0s/wheel_a_steady=30.0mm/s^2 are design-choice placeholders (tens-of-seconds adaptation per the issue's own text; a steady-gate conservatively below planner.a_max=300mm/s^2), bench-verified in ticket 006, not yet re-verified on hardware. Stage B (fast PID) and the deficit-flag policy ship MECHANISM-ONLY, INERT (every wheel_pid_*/wheel_deficit_* key held at 0): Open Question 4 (does the fast loop need a nonzero kp at all, given the profiler's every-tick re-plan-from-measured-position) is an explicit bench judgment call this ticket cannot make -- tovez is hard-silent (clasi/issues/tovez-hard-silent-i2c-wedge-blocks-completing-the-population-duty-sweep.md) and untunable this session. wheel_pid_kaff's natural non-zero starting value, once Stage B is bench-tuned, is planner.plant_tau (0.23s) verbatim -- wheel_trim.h's own convention: kaff IS the plant time constant, not half of it (unlike the superseded planner-side trim's now-parked trim_kaff=plant_tau/2). 130-006 BENCH VERIFIED (2026-08-02, tovez, firmware v0.20260801.18, src/tests/bench/wheel_controller_ab_bench.py): Stage C's bias adaptation is CONFIRMED LIVE and CORRECTLY CONVERGING -- a continuous 90s wheels() hold at cmd 150mm/s (no intermediate estop(), see src/tests/bench/output/bias_convergence_150.png) showed biasRight climbing smoothly 0->+14.0mm/s and biasLeft settling near -3 to -5mm/s, both well inside the +-23.8mm/s clamp (never saturated; deficit flags never latched), measured velocity converging to within ~5mm/s of 150mm/s by t~15-20s. estop() resets bias to exactly 0 by design (ticket 004) -- the SHORT-hold residual sweep this same session (4x 6s holds at cmd 100/150/250/400, each ending in estop()) therefore measures the fresh-start/instantaneous response (L 79-85%/R 70-80% of commanded), NOT the converged one; 6s is 20% of tauAdapt, nowhere near settled. The +500 button (run_unmanaged_distance_drive(), always starts from bias=0) was re-verified end-to-end against the 06-issue's acceptance spec: endpoint criteria PASS (elapsed 3.85s, encoders 510/502mm vs 500+-15mm, L/R split 8mm, taper reaches the 90mm/s floor without either wheel hitting zero); transient criteria FAIL at shipped (Stage B=0) gains -- rise 0.59s (bound <=0.3s), ripple 24/23mm/s (bound <=10), max L-R split 21mm/s (bound <=10). A one-shot Stage B trial (kp=0.3/ki=0.02/iMax=20/kaff=0.23=plant_tau/pidMax=30) cut rise to 0.18s (clears the bound) but WORSENED ripple (34mm/s) and left the L-R split unclosed (20mm/s) -- reverted live (config(pid.kp=0,...)) rather than keep a mixed result; a real Stage B tuning sweep (not one trial point) is the recommended next step, filed as a follow-up issue. Separately: this session's saturation reading (L 571.7/R 532.5mm/s at full duty) and residual-sweep percentages both measure LOWER than ab303ee3's own 2026-07-31 baseline (L 760-795/R 696 saturation; ~94-99%/70-86% residual) -- an unexplained ~20-25% apparent plant-gain drop since that measurement, flagged but NOT root-caused this session (no pack-voltage telemetry to confirm or rule out a battery-state difference between sessions). Full data: src/tests/bench/output/wheel_controller_ab_bench.{csv,png}, bias_convergence_150.{csv,png}.

planner._align_note: 134-003 terminal fine-align (docs/bench-reports/motion-planning-lab-2026-08-04.md §5.2 and §3). align_tol is 1.0 DEGREE expressed in radians -- the report's operating point, converted once here because every angular field downstream (Motion::PlannerLimits::Landing, this robot's own settle_rest_omega/settle_epsilon_angular) is radians. MEASURED, not chosen: 333 individual trim nudges on this robot showed the low-speed corrective pivot is bimodal -- 26% deliver <0.25 deg (no breakaway), the rest a median 1.72 deg (10th pct 0.63 deg) -- so a tolerance below that ~1.8 deg quantum is outside the mechanism's own authority. At 0.3 deg, corner convergence drops 93%->64%, nudge cost triples, ~14 s/tour is added, and some corners get WORSE (a nudge fires at a residual it cannot resolve); closure is indistinguishable (0.3 deg vs 1.0 deg: 11.5 vs 9.4 mm planner, 7.9 vs 9.1 mm wheels). At 1.0 deg: 1.3 nudges/corner, ~2 s/corner, 94% convergence, tours at ~8-11 mm against 64 mm uncorrected. DO NOT TIGHTEN THIS if a tour number disappoints -- that is the one response the data has already ruled out. The road below ~8 mm is a finer terminal actuator (report §5.4), not a finer threshold. align_max_nudges = 6 matches the proven host-side graft's own default (src/tests/bench/planner_square_tour.py) so firmware and the measurement agree by construction.
planner._domain_note: 129-009 (config consolidation): Motion::Planner limits+gains, MOVED HERE from a C++ literal block main.cpp assembled directly (2026-07-26 integration) -- same values, new home, no behavior change. Plant ID 2026-07-26 (square_tour_sim.py tourLimits() / on-robot tour): gain ~1370 mm/s per duty, tau ~230 ms (plant_gain/plant_tau below, kept as recorded measured data -- 130-009 removed the last PlannerLimits fields derived from them). NOT the retired control.vel_*/a_max/... blocks above -- those fed the deleted NezhaMotor MotorVelocityPid and Motion::VelocityShaper (itself also since deleted).
planner._timing_note: control_period/actuation_delay: BOTH ARE "= App::RobotLoop::kCycle" BY CONSTRUCTION -- not separately-measured numbers. control_period is the loop interval one planner tick() plans for; actuation_delay is one control period because a command staged this cycle lands on the wheels the next one (src/firm/motion/planner/tests/planner_noise_test.cpp: 'command lands one cycle late'). If kCycle changes, BOTH change with it, in every robot JSON. HISTORY: 130-007 set one 50ms control period everywhere when kCycle was raised 40->50 (the older 47ms was the MEASURED delivered period at kCycle=40, ~7ms of vendor-bus-clearance overrun the nominal did not include -- three dishonest numbers for one physical quantity). 130-011 bench re-measurement then found delivered was 54ms, not 50, with cycleBusy only ~21-23ms -- so NOT a budget overrun. 131-005 root-caused it: each of the four runAndWait() pacing blocks computed its wait as a GAP from its OWN entry mark, so each  block's rounding was re-added on top of the next block's fixed budget instead of being absorbed; cycle()'s trailing block now targets an ABSOLUTE end-of-cycle deadline (cycleStart+kCycle). That fix was proven in a host-build jitter test but left an open hardware follow-up. FOLLOW-UP CLOSED (2026-08-07, tovez, direct serial): delivered cycle_period measures 50.00ms median, min 49.97, max 50.06. The pacer works; delivered == nominal. UPDATED 50.0 -> 32.0 (2026-08-07, out of process, same session): the loop was paced far slower than its own work needs. Measured floor (kCycle set BELOW the floor so the trailing sleepUntil yields and the delivered period becomes the true work time) was 22.2ms median as shipped, and 17.7ms once the post-duty-write kClear window was removed as provably-dead padding. 32 is chosen against the TAIL, not the median: worst-case cycles run ~28ms in every configuration measured, so 32 preserves delivered == nominal by construction rather than buying a faster median at the cost of occasionally-stretched cycles. Verified at exactly this period on tovez: 32.00ms median, max 32.04. The planner's discrete math (accel steps, braking sums, ramp tick counts) uses the period the loop actually delivers; telemetry cycle_period re-measures it on every frame if the schedule ever changes again.
planner._settle_note: settle_rest_velocity/settle_rest_omega are sized to the measured hardware encoder-velocity noise (plant ID 2026-07-26: ~+-7mm/s at rest) -- the rest-damping stage outputs exactly zero duty below the floor, so it must clear the noise band or the wheels twitch at rest forever. settle_epsilon_linear/settle_epsilon_angular are arrival tolerances sized to the stiction-limited creep resolution (the demonstrated one-sided-creep resolution: single-turn probe 2026-07-27 landed +1.76deg; the right wheel does not reverse under the breakaway kick, so fine correction rides the left wheel). heading_hold_gain: WAS 2.0 ('sim-validated', never bench-validated); ZEROED 130-011 (2026-08-02) -- Planner::applyHeadingHold() is a P-loop on pure-encoder heading (OTOS blend fail-closed to 0.0 everywhere), i.e. closing the loop on a delayed function of its own output. Bench-reproduced as a sustained ~1Hz wheel-reversal limit cycle on an ordinary straight move_twist() leg at the new 54ms actual period (isolated single-leg A/B: gain=2.0 oscillates and takes 11.35s for a 500mm leg that should take ~4s; gain=0.0 is clean) -- App::Drive's own raw wheels() path was unaffected in both conditions, isolating the bug to this correction, not the 130-004/005/007 wheel-speed controller. togov.json/tovez_nocal.json carry the same 2.0 and are NOT independently bench-confirmed unstable (no hardware there this session) but share the same code path -- treat as equally suspect. 130-009 removed require_settle/settle_window (the settle-confirm DEFER path they gated, already dissolved by 130-008's Settling-state deletion) and the M4 duty-stage/trim keys the notes below used to document -- see boot_config.h's PlannerBootConfig doc comment for the removal rationale. RE-ENABLED 0.0 -> 1.0 (2026-08-13, out of process, playfield): the ZEROED rationale above is STALE and must not be re-applied as written. It rests on 'a P-loop on pure-encoder heading ... closing the loop on a delayed function of its own output', which was true on 2026-08-02 when PoseTracker still blended OTOS in by a weight that was fail-closed to 0.0 everywhere. 130-009 then DELETED that weighted blend (blendHeading(), PlannerLimits::headingOtosWeight/otosStaleness) and replaced it with a hard override -- Motion::PoseTracker::heading() (motion/planner/estimation.h) now returns `otosActive_ ? otosHeading_ : heading_`, so whenever the chip is connected and fresh, pose_.heading() IS the OTOS heading and the encoder value is not consulted at all. applyHeadingHold() therefore no longer closes on its own output; it closes on an independent sensor, which is precisely the condition the 130-011 diagnosis said was missing. MEASURED on the playfield 2026-08-13 against overhead-camera truth (median-of-7 rest fixes, 6 straight 300mm legs + 4 in-place turns): OTOS heading tracked camera truth to 0.82 deg mean absolute error, and encoder heading to 1.05 deg once its inverted sign convention is accounted for -- i.e. BOTH sensors see the veer, so the veer was never a sensing failure, it was heading_hold_gain=0 leaving nothing to act on a signal the robot already had. Uncorrected veer over a single 300mm leg measured 5.6 deg mean / 18.7 deg worst case, same sign in both travel directions (so NOT a wheel-gain asymmetry, which would flip sign in reverse). 1.0 is deliberately conservative against the 2.0 that oscillated: a P-loop on an integrator with this loop's ~0.2s total delay has a stability limit near pi/(2*T) ~ 7.8, so 1.0 keeps wide margin while the re-enable is re-validated on hardware. If this oscillates again, the thing to check FIRST is whether otosActive_ is actually latching (telemetry flags bit 0 / bit 1) -- with a dead or disconnected OTOS this correction silently reverts to exactly the encoder self-feedback loop 130-011 condemned. NOTE also that weight_heading_otos/otos_untrusted elsewhere in this file are DEAD KEYS with no firmware consumer (ESTIMATOR's install() is permanently ERR_UNIMPLEMENTED); they are not what enables the OTOS here and setting them does nothing.

navigator._navigator_note: 135-004: seeded from Motion::NavigatorLimits' own compile-time defaults (src/firm/motion/navigator/arc_solver.h, tickets 002/003) -- speed/max_wheel_step/behind_angle/turn_first_angle/approach_radius/approach_speed/default_arrival_tolerance are the SAME values that struct already shipped with, now sourced from this file instead of a C++ default (configuration-discipline.md). approach_radius/approach_speed=0 leaves the near-target speed taper disabled, matching every existing ctest/bench script. track_width is deliberately NOT a key here -- NavigatorLimits::trackWidth is derived from this file's own geometry.trackwidth/rotational_slip (Config::Robot::effectiveTrackWidth()), never a second, independently-tunable copy of the same physical fact. yaw_sign=-1.0 is NOT a placeholder: it is src/tests/bench/goto_otos.py's own measured YAW_SIGN ("commanded omega is opposite to world CCW (measured)", and the same figure otos_scale_run.py/turn_accuracy.py/otos_drift.py/goto_world.py independently agree on for this robot) -- see NavigatorLimits::yawSign's own doc comment (navigator.h) for the full derivation of why Motion::Navigator needs this correction and why no sim/ctest plant can validate it. Ticket 006's own bench pass is the re-verification of this SAME already-measured fact against the new GO_TO wire arm, not a fresh discovery. default_arrival_tolerance 100.0 -> 10.0 (2026-08-13, out of process, playfield, camera truth): 100 mm was the DOMINANT GO_TO error term -- the Navigator declares arrival as soon as it is within this radius, so a GO_TO legitimately stopped up to 10 cm short and then sat there. Traced directly: a 350 mm ROBOT-frame target drove smoothly, stopped at 303.6 mm, and held that position for 11 s. Measured arrival error (ROBOT-frame targets, displacement expressed in the start body frame, median-of-7 rest fixes, 4 targets per run): tolerance 100 -> mean 76 mm with outliers to 271 mm; tolerance 10 -> mean 12.7 mm, max 17.7 mm; tolerance 3 -> mean 12.6 mm, max 21.8 mm (NO further gain, so 10 is at the knee, not on a slope); baked 10 as the default -> mean 15.8 mm, max 23.0 mm. approach_radius/approach_speed were also trialled at 150 mm / 60 mm/s to taper the final approach and made no difference (mean 13.5 mm), so they are deliberately left at 0/disabled rather than shipped unvalidated. The residual ~12-15 mm floor is NOT the tolerance and NOT the taper: it is consistent with the robot arriving accurately in its OWN frame and carrying ~2 deg of heading error, which is this drivetrain's own documented terminal stiction quantum (planner._align_note) and puts ~14 mm of lateral error on a 400 mm leg. Closing that needs a finer terminal actuator or a camera-in-the-loop correction, not a smaller tolerance.

otos._otos_linear_scale_note: 2026-08-05, TAPE-measured on the playfield, robot untethered (battery + gauti). Supersedes the 2026-07-30 (126-003) value of 1.0275, which was camera-anchored and is therefore invalid: the overhead camera overstates the ROBOT's displacement by ~11-12% because tag 100 sits 12cm above the playfield plane (registered z_cm=12.0) and the height correction is not landing -- flat tags 12/14/15/16 on the same field read true to ~1cm, so it is the elevated tag only, not the playfield calibration. Method: linear_scale pushed to 1.0 (verified by read-back), world pose seeded from the camera, one 1000mm leg, then a human tape measure chord start-to-end. Raw OTOS read 971.7mm against 990mm of tape => 990/971.7 = 1.0188. Verified on two further legs, opposite directions: 900mm commanded read 895.0mm, and a repeat 1000mm leg read 992.0mm against 990mm of tape (+0.2%, inside the tape's own reading precision). The camera read 1109.7 / 1000.7 / 1110.0mm on those same three legs -- precise to 0.3mm on a repeat, but biased +12%, which is what a geometric height error looks like as opposed to noise. NOTE this also falsifies the long-standing 'robot over-delivers distance 1.10-1.14x' finding: the planner delivers 1000mm as 990mm (1%), and the over-delivery was the camera all along.

estimator._estimator_note: 117 (predict-to-now estimator v1): weight_heading_otos/weight_omega_otos committed 0.0 -- stakeholder's encoder-only-v1 decision, OTOS fusion is wired but not yet trusted with any nonzero weight. staleness_ms=60.0 is 3x Devices::Otos::kReadPeriod (20ms): generous headroom over the OTOS chip's own read cadence, small enough to exclude a genuinely stale reading before the next cycle's fresh one arrives. (118 ticket 004, land-at-zero-completion-delete-stop-lead.md: this section's own former fourth key -- a boot-time anticipation-lead constant with a four-retune history and no stable value -- is DELETED; the mechanism it fed no longer exists, see App::MoveQueue::tick()'s own doc comment for the land-at-zero completion predicate that replaces it.)

perception._note: Sensor mount geometry, BODY FRAME, stakeholder-supplied 2026-08-08. x is FORWARD of the wheel axis, y is LEFT-positive (ROS REP-103, the same convention the playfield camera's CCW-positive yaw uses), origin at the centre of rotation -- the same point tag 100 is registered to. Consumed HOST-side for lever-arm compensation (src/tests/bench/field_map.py); the firmware does not need and does not read these, which is why this block is not in the wire config or the generator.
perception._units_note: UNIT CORRECTION, flagged not silently applied: the colour offset was given as '48 cm in front of the wheel axis'. 480 mm would put the sensor 3.75 track-widths (trackwidth = 128 mm) ahead of the robot, which is physically impossible, and 48 mm is the consistent sibling of the line array's stated 96 mm. Recorded as 48 mm. Correct this if the intent really was centimetres.

line_array._offsets_note: Lateral offsets from the centre line, Lego stud pitch 8 mm: inner pair at +/-8 mm (one hole), outer pair at +/-32 mm (four holes). The outer pair was described as '14 off' AND as '32 mm'; 14 studs is 112 mm and 14 mm is not a hole multiple, so the explicit 32 mm is used. 32 mm = 4 studs exactly, which is self-consistent.
line_array._channel_order_note: VERIFIED 2026-08-08 (stakeholder): sensor 1 is the LEFT-most, sensor 4 the RIGHT-most. Body frame y is left-positive, so channel_y descends left-to-right as listed. This was previously unverified and called out as the one input that could silently MIRROR the whole map -- it is now confirmed to be correct as written.
